messages:
julie: @devon incoming escalation from Acme Health — their production traffic is getting repeated 503/gateway errors since ~06:10 UTC. They pasted one sample: `{'error':'UpstreamError','status':503,'request_id':'r-9f2c'}`. Customer is seeing user-facing failures.

devon: looking. quick check of router logs shows repeated 502/503 from the inference gateway with upstream worker exits. I see pods in namespace redwood-hosted-infer restarting. Pod logs show both `OOMKilled` and `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` around the same times.

eli: which model/variant is this hitting? large seqs?

julie: model: gpt-open-13b-v2 (quantized q4_8bit). Traffic pattern: some bursty batch spikes (client sends many simultaneous small reqs, our router batches them) — batch sizes went from 4 -> 20+ for a short window. Some requests have seq_len ~4096, a few at ~8192.

devon: ok that matches GPU mem pressure. paste from one worker log:

```
2026-02-28T06:11:03Z runtime: allocate_kv_cache 256MB -> success
2026-02-28T06:11:04Z runtime: GPU memory usage 95% (11.4Gi/12.0Gi)
2026-02-28T06:11:04Z runtime: spawning inference thread
2026-02-28T06:11:05Z runtime: segfault at 0x7f2c1a... (signal 11)
[1]    12345 segmentation fault  /opt/infer/bin/runtime
kubelet: pod "infer-rt-5f9d7" terminated: OOMKilled
```

eli: SIGSEGV + OOM together often means kernel attempted a large allocation (big batch + long seq) and either the allocation failed or a bug in the quantized kernel surfaced under memory pressure. We also have a couple recent commits to the allocator — could be a regression but need to triage as OOM-first.

maria: customer says this is intermittent and mainly during peak minutes. They want ETA for fix, asking to know if we can throttle or give them a workaround.

devon: immediate mitigations we can push: 1) limit router batch_size to 8 for that model/route, 2) reduce max_seq_length to 4096 temporarily via model config override, 3) enable fallback to a CPU variant or lower-memory model for that customer (if configured), 4) restart the affected node pool to clear leaked memory.

sre-bot: auto-scaler triggered restart of node-group-hosted-gpu-3 at 06:12 due to repeated pod failures. 2/3 pods replaced.

ops-bot: applied runtime flag `--max-batch=8` on route `/v1/generate` for model `gpt-open-13b-v2` at 06:20 UTC (rolled out to 30% canary).

julie: pushed those mitigations to customer and asked for patience. customer accepted temporary throttling.

eli: repro steps for engineering: 
1) send parallel 24 requests with seq_len=8192 simulating client burst: 
```
for i in `seq 1 24`; do \
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-13b-v2","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1024}' &
done; wait
```
This reproduces the OOM on dev cluster with similar capacity.

devon: logs from kube describe pod show repeated exit code 137/OOMKilled then a segmentation fault when runtime restarts quickly. Suggest we give runtime a clean restart (grace period) instead of immediate restart back-to-back — uses kube restart policy window.

eli: quick root-cause candidates: 1) allocator wrong math for q4 pack size under certain batch+seq combos, 2) regression in attention kernel causing invalid memory access under high occupancy, 3) lack of pre-check to refuse batches that would exceed device capacity.

maria: customer-facing note: "We applied temporary throttles and reduced max sequence length for your traffic; this should cut the 503s. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a postmortem."

julie: action items assigned: 
- devon: monitor infra and keep throttles in place; revert only if safe (assigned)
- eli: reproduce locally, bisect recent allocator/quantization commits (assigned)
- devon/eli: add pre-allocation check to refuse/break batches that would overflow GPU; add safer fallback path (assigned)
- maria: keep customer updated (assigned)

devon: quick patch applied 06:45 UTC: runtime now rejects batch > 16 for this model at the dispatcher level and gracefully falls back to CPU for that request instead of crashing. Rolling restart scheduled across affected nodes.

ops-bot: rolling restart started at 06:52 UTC (10 pods). Drain schedule: 10m per pod.

eli: I pushed a reproducer and a narrowed diff — allocator math fixed in PR #4821, removing an unsafe cast that undercounted required bytes for packed KV cache. I'll open the PR for review now.

sre-bot: incident severity set to P1 -> escalated to on-call SRE.

julie: ETA to customer: we'll send a follow-up in 2 hours with root cause & next steps. For now customer-facing fix in place.

maria: customer acknowledged, says they saw errors drop drastically after the throttles. will ping if anything else pops up.

devon: postmortem owner? eli willing to own the RCA and mitigation PRs. assigning to eli.

eli: I'll draft the postmortem and include timeline + recommended long-term changes: smarter pre-checks, safer fallbacks, a regression test in CI simulating high-batch+long-seq, and a canary for allocator changes.

julie: thanks team. leaving monitoring on for 24h and will file follow-up ticket for billing customers impacted to ensure no unexpected charges due to retries. :thumbsup:
